title: Signed interchange of the two strict Roos directions
statement: Let C, R, the existing complex and tower categories, rows, columns, and their specified coordinate and evaluation maps be as in [def-sp-signed-double-roos-tensor-exchange-data]. For every strict double inverse sequence of unbounded complexes, there is a natural chain isomorphism beta from rows to columns whose composite with columnCoordinate(p,q,k,n,j) is rowCoordinate(p,q,k,n,j), negated exactly if both p and q are true. The two evaluation squares commute: beta followed by Roos(innerEvaluation of the flipped tower at n) is evaluation at n of the row tower, and beta followed by evaluation at j of the column tower is Roos(innerEvaluation at j). No exactness, boundedness, torsion or regularity hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Put $P^a=\prod_n\prod_jX_{n,j}^a$ and let $A=1-s_n$, $B=1-s_j$ on $P$. Define the product interchange by requiring its $(j,n)$ projection to equal the original $(n,j)$ projection. The reversed prescription is inverse, since every projection of either composite is the corresponding projection of the identity. Strict commutation of the transitions gives $AB=BA$ by the same projection test. We also use the canonical identification $\prod_i(M_i\oplus N_i)\cong(\prod_iM_i)\oplus(\prod_iN_i)$: send a pair of product vectors to its pairs of projections; the inverse has first and second components the products of the two biproduct projections. Both composites are identities on all components. These constructions commute with component maps and differentials. Thus the two iterated Roos complexes may be expanded using the same $P$.

proof.text:
In total degree $k$, expand the source $\mathsf R_n\mathsf R_jX$ in the order $(a,b,c,h)$ of Roos degrees $(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$. Its four summands are $P^k,P^{k-1},P^{k-1},P^{k-2}$. Apply the differential $(dv,-du-(1-s)v)$ twice. The result is
$$D(a,b,c,h)=(da,-db-Ba,-dc-Aa,dh+Bc-Ab).$$
For example the last component is the negative of the second component of the inner differential on $(c,h)$, minus $A$ applied to $b$, namely $dh+Bc-Ab$. This also fixes the sign of the doubly shifted coordinate without any totalization convention left implicit.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, applied twice with the shift sign

proof.text:
The target order is $(j\text{-degree},n\text{-degree})$. Define $\beta(a,b,c,h)=(a,c,b,-h)$ after the product interchange. Using step 2 with $A,B$ exchanged, both $D\beta$ and $\beta D$ have components
$$(da,-dc-Aa,-db-Ba,-dh-Bc+Ab).$$
Thus $\beta$ is a chain map. Its reversed-coordinate formula is its inverse. It is exactly multiplication by $(-1)^{pq}$ on bidegree $(p,q)$, with no sign on the other three coordinates.

For a strict double-tower map, the induced maps on the four coordinates are the respective product maps; these commute with permutation, negation, and both shifts. This proves naturality. Evaluation at $n$ in the outer source retains $(a,b)$ and projects their $n$ index. In the target it retains the coordinates with $n$-Roos degree zero, also $(a,b)$ after $\beta$. Evaluation at $j$ likewise retains $(a,c)$ on either side. The sign on $h$ never enters either evaluation. Hence both evaluation squares commute as chain-map squares.

lean.statement: theorem signed_double_roos_interchange_core : ∃ β : rows R ≅ columns R, (∀ (X : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Tower R) (p q : Bool) (k : ℤ) (n j : ℕ), (β.hom.app X).f k ≫ columnCoordinate R X p q k n j = if p && q then -rowCoordinate R X p q k n j else rowCoordinate R X p q k n j) ∧ (∀ (X : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Tower R) (n : ℕ), β.hom.app X ≫ (roos R).map (innerEvaluation R X.flip n) = evaluation R (X ⋙ roos R) n) ∧ (∀ (X : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Tower R) (j : ℕ), β.hom.app X ≫ evaluation R (X.flip ⋙ roos R) j = (roos R).map (innerEvaluation R X j))
